title: Choose the visual world for the DepTrace dashboard
question: The roll assigned Catalog Cards. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Catalog Cards
options.lineage: library card catalogs and ruled index cards
options.thesis: Every module is a catalog card: a call number, cross-references in, cross-references out.
options.viewport: Oak-toned side rail, overview metrics on ruled white panels, the selected module open as a red-ruled card beside the graph.
options.risk: Can tip into nostalgia if the red rule and ruled lines spread beyond the card itself.

raised.raise: Structure is drawn only with 1px hairlines; no shadows, no floating cards.
Focusing a module dims everything it does not touch.
One depth control drives the whole graph's transitive highlight live.

options.label: Survey Strata
options.lineage: geological survey maps and stratigraphic columns
options.thesis: Layers are strata; a boundary violation is a fault line cutting across them.
options.viewport: A stratigraphic column of the configured layers beside the metrics; violations drawn as red faults across the bands.
options.risk: Earth tints compete with severity colours and can read muted in dark mode.

options.label: Night Network
options.thesis: Every dependency path is a line you can ride: files are stations, layers are line colours.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue shell; the graph centre stage; a selected path or cycle drawn as a line strip with station ticks, coloured by layer.
options.case: Wins both axes: developers already read dependency paths as routes, and layer-coloured lines make layers legible everywhere.
options.risk: Line inks cap distinct layer colours near six; the graph layout itself is not an orthogonal metro map.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Findings are a board ranked by severity; anything new stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: Violations board leads, rows in a fixed column grid; new-versus-baseline rows hold the amber alert.
options.case: Strong for the reviewer's baseline question; weaker as a home for the graph.
options.risk: Split-flap pastiche if the board styling leaks past the findings table.

options.label: Lexicon Plates
options.thesis: Text stays black; colour lives only inside bordered plates: the graph and the charts.
options.viewport: Monochrome shell and lists with guide words naming the span in view; the graph sits as the one colour plate.
options.case: Colour quarantine makes data colour unmistakable; the shoulder margin costs width on dense screens.
options.risk: Can read like a document rather than a tool.

options.label: Annual Plates
options.thesis: The graph as a registered plate on near-white stock.
options.case: Loses both axes: developers do not read their code as gallery plates.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Modules as rows of tiles that grow on focus.
options.viewport: Rows of module tiles by layer.
options.case: Loses both axes: tiles hide the relationships that are the whole point.
options.risk: Entertainment framing for an engineering task.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider remaps the whole page live.
options.viewport: Giant display type over a module grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: typography is not this product's subject.
options.kept: One continuous control driving the whole view.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral dark developer-tool dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Side nav, metric row, graph and tables in the arrangement developers expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other developer dashboards by design.
